summary.headline: NRB Bearings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% YoY to INR386 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 18.2% and PAT of INR36 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR386 crore, up 18.8% YoY (19% for H1), with adjusted EBITDA of INR71 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR36 crore. Growth was described as broad-based across automotive, exports, industrial and new products, with Industrial stated to have grown 48% and CV up 47%. Management steered investors toward EBITDA and operating EBITDA rather than PAT, citing depreciation from capacity build-out. Capacity additions (Unitec JV at Aurangabad, Mahant Tool Room aerospace push) were positioned as the next growth leg, with guidance kept qualitative.

financial_highlights.value: 47% (Q2 per prepared remarks); 40%+ per analyst paraphrase

segments.name: Automotive (CV, two/three-wheelers, passenger cars, farm)
segments.commentary: Management said growth was across all segments including LCV, MCV, HCV, two/three-wheelers, passenger cars and farm equipment; CV grew 47%. Two-wheelers and CVs described as resilient double-digit demand.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 48% YoY, versus a 34% figure management had earlier indicated. Industrial focus includes industrial gearboxes via the Unitec JV.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Growth of 16%+ in constant currency terms, described as back on a growth trajectory.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Typically grows 9-12%, per management; not pursued at the expense of margin.

segments.name: Mahant Tool Room (aerospace and defence)
segments.commentary: Acquired company with INR2.5 crore turnover base; Q2 sales INR55 lakh. Management targets INR1 crore per quarter in roughly nine months to a year; 2031 target of INR300 crore cited by analyst, not reconfirmed in detail.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give formal forward guidance but said 19% growth is sustainable and it intends to sustain and surpass it once a new growth threshold is reached.
Management said it aims to maintain EBITDA as a percentage of sales in the 17-18% range, per its prior-call framing, and to protect margins.
Growth trajectory expected to step up roughly every six months as new capacity comes on stream; management said not Q1 or Q2 specifically.

Unitec JV at Aurangabad expected to commission on track by April 2027; revenue breakup for FY28 not provided. An analyst cited INR130 crore revenue potential; management said full utilisation in FY28 is not expected.
Mahant Tool Room: growth expected to come in years four and five; business from new bearing certifications takes a minimum of 18 months.
capex_capacity: Unitec JV at Aurangabad on track for commissioning by April 2027 (per analyst question; management confirmed on track).
Capacity is largely common: about 60-70% of capacity is common across two/three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, tractors and industrial, with 20-30% dedicated.
Management said capacity is being added against orders already firmly in place, with new facilities, products and certifications under way at Mahant Tool Room.
Mahant Tool Room holds AS9100D and product certifications; management said no further certifications are required for the MTR product range.
Management said the company does not have adequate capacity for the growth opportunities ahead, and that depreciation from capacity build-out weighs on PAT.
demand_pricing: Management said customers are consolidating supplier bases toward co-development partners; new products priced to reflect current input-cost realities and customers are supporting it.
Management said it is deliberately exiting commoditised lines such as two-wheeler bearings where competitors' margins are hit, and pivoting to differentiated high-margin products.
Customer concentration: management said no single customer is above 10% of sales; top 10 customers include Magna, ZF and Daimler per management.
Management claims about 30% global market share in truck bearings and about 30% in two-wheeler bearings.
Receivables: management said DSO is at the same level as before, which it considers healthy given high growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is 19% H1 growth sustainable against the ~15% guidance, and will EBITDA keep growing faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 19% growth is sustainable and it aims to sustain and surpass it, but declined to give forward guidance. It said it intends to maintain EBITDA as a percentage of sales rather than commit to EBITDA growth outpacing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Unitec JV be commissioned by April 2027, what FY28 revenue is expected, and will the full capacity be used?
qa_highlights.answer: On track for commissioning, but no revenue breakup given at this stage. Management said full utilisation in FY28 is not expected for a new division.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 19% YoY, and will growth trajectory be similar going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COGS rose only about 1%, citing cost management and product mix. It acknowledged power, fuel, logistics and input cost pressures in other expenses, which it expects to offset with higher growth as capacity comes in. It referred back to its five-year strategy rather than a specific growth number.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments underperformed, and is the BMW steering win global?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all segments grew. Commoditised two-wheeler products are deliberately deprioritised. Management said the new BMW steering business starts from January and BMW manufactures on a global platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is non-auto revenue in H1 and the FY30 target; what is the industrial vs aerospace/defence revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a split, saying company definitions of auto differ and NRB's auto definition is the widest, including CVs and two/three-wheelers. It cited a 48% industrial growth rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is Mahant Tool Room's Q2 contribution, path from INR30 crore order book to INR300 crore revenue by 2031, and dependence on HAL?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 sales were INR55 lakh. Management said MTR is moving from about INR2.5 crore turnover toward INR1 crore per quarter in nine months to a year, with growth in years four and five. New bearing business takes at least 18 months, and management did not give HAL dependence figures.

qa_highlights.question: Who benefits from aerospace bearing shortages over the next 18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NRB supplies critical parts for Sukhoi and commercial aircraft, including plain spherical bearings made by very few global firms, and that global peers have sold off aerospace plants due to customisation limits.

risks_watch: Depreciation from new capacity will keep PAT growth lagging revenue and EBITDA; management asked investors to focus on EBITDA instead.
Input-cost pressure (power, fuel, logistics) is rising within other expenses, which management said will be offset by growth.
Receivables/DSO and export receivables: an analyst asked about a possible strain tied to a war scenario; management said DSO is flat.
Mahant Tool Room execution: 18-month lead time for bearing certifications and business wins, and revenue ramp only in years four and five.
Unitec JV commissioning by April 2027 and utilisation ramp in FY28; no revenue breakup disclosed.
Forex and dividend income from SNL are excluded from operational view by management but affect reported PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on strategy and capability, but evasive on hard numbers: no segment revenue split, no formal guidance, and no clear answers on other expenses or the non-auto definition. Management repeatedly emphasised conservatism and redirected PAT questions to EBITDA.
key_quotes: Our adjusted EBITDA is INR71 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 18.2%.
Please look at our results from the viewpoint of capacity and capability expansion.
We buy access and speed, not capacity.
We are 30% of global market share for truck, which matches our 30% of global market share for two-wheelers.

Mahant Tool Room new facilities and product certifications under way (aerospace/defence)

growth.why: Management declined formal guidance but said 19% growth is sustainable and it expects a step-up in growth roughly every six months as capacity comes on stream, backed by the Unitec JV (commissioning on track by April 2027) and capacity added against firm orders, though no quantified revenue breakup was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said it intends to hold EBITDA at 17-18% of sales (Q2 adjusted margin 18.2%) and COGS rose only ~1% vs revenue +18.8%, but other expenses (power, fuel, logistics) rose ~19% and it did not commit to margin expansion, so this is a hold rather than an expansion call.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unitec JV at Aurangabad is under construction and management confirmed commissioning on track by April 2027; Mahant Tool Room facilities and certifications are also under way (MTR revenue target INR1 crore/quarter in 9-12 months).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 18.8% in Q2 and 19% in H1; management called 19% sustainable and expects a step-up in growth roughly every six months as capacity comes on stream, though no quantified volume guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it does not have adequate capacity for growth ahead and is building (not pre-building) capacity against firm orders, with Unitec JV still ramping; no new capex amount or utilisation figure was disclosed, so the timing is inferred rather than guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined formal forward guidance but said 19% growth is sustainable and it intends to sustain and surpass it once a higher growth threshold is reached, with a step-up expected in about six months.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Other-expense inflation (power, fuel, logistics up ~19%), depreciation from new capacity weighing on PAT, and Mahant Tool Room's slow 18-month certification lead time are the main risks; no explicit cut was signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New BMW steering business starts from January and new products are being priced and supported by customers; MTR new bearing certifications take at least 18 months, so aerospace launches fall later in the window.

rows.label: BMW steering business start
rows.why: Management said the new BMW steering business starts from January, with BMW manufacturing on a global platform.

rows.label: Mahant Tool Room ramp to INR1 crore per quarter
rows.why: MTR Q2 sales were INR55 lakh against a ~INR2.5 crore turnover base and a INR30 crore order book; the INR300 crore 2031 target was cited by an analyst and not reconfirmed in detail, and growth is expected only in years four and five.

rows.label: Exit of commoditised two-wheeler lines
rows.why: Management is deliberately exiting commoditised lines such as two-wheeler bearings, where competitor margins are hit, and pivoting to high-margin products, supporting mix and margin.
